newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed little changed at 8.2906 on Friday from Thursday's 8.2908 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a lack of fresh market-moving stimuli, traders said.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2910.
The yuan opened down at 8.2915 and rose slightly to move in a narrow range of 8.2907 and 8.2910 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2901 and a low of 8.2939.
Trading was active early in the session but dull late in trading with most business done at 8.2908, traders said.
Dealers said the yuan gained support at about 8.2910 on Friday but buyers seemed to have no intention to pushed it above the key 8.2900 resistance level.
"Despite the low opening, buying was heavy below the 8.2910 level," one trader said. "There was one deal which made the yuan hit an intraday low of 8.2939 but it had no impact on the market."
"Buyers had no intention to push the yuan above the 8.2900 level, afraid a sharp rise in the yuan would trigger central bank intervention," a second trader said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move narrowly around the current level in dull trading on Saturday.
The exchange will trade on Saturday because it will close from Sunday to Tuesday on a public holiday to mark the Hong Kong takeover, exchange officials said.
The yuan closed down at 7.2951 from 7.2518 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at an intraday low of 1.0706 from 1.0695 against the Hong Kong dollar.
